changed_pages.previous_text: 7 1 Introduction and background 1.1 Introduction This report presents the findings of the UgIFT asset verification undertaken by the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development as part of programme closure activities. It sets out the status of the assets provided by the programme to the target ed national institutions responsible for supporting the implementation of the programme, Blood Banks and local governments specifically targeting Seed Secondary Schools and health facilities upgraded from Health Centre II to Health Centre III. 1.2 Background to the verification The Uganda Intergovernmental Fiscal Transfers (UgIFT) Programme is a government programme implemented through a Programme -for-Results (PforR) launched and aligned with the broader IGFT Reform Programme (2015). UgIFT 1.0 began with US$200 million in FY2017/ 18, supporting Education and Health. This was later expanded through additional financing of US$300 million, including US$240 million in credit and US$60 million in grants, with US$50 million from the IDA Refugee Support Window, expanding beyond Education and Health to water and Environment and Agriculture (micro-scale irrigation) making the overall funding total of US$500 million. The Intergovernmental Fiscal Transfer Reform Programme (IGFT RP) was revised in 2020 to align with the Third National Development Plan (NDP III 2020/21 - 2024/25), and to directly contribute to Four (04) Programmes i.e. Human Capital Development; Public Se ctor Transformation; Natural Resources, Environment, Climate change, Land and Water Management; and Development Plan Implementation. Overall, the development objective of the UgIFT Programme was to: “Improve the adequacy, equity, and effectiveness of financing and the oversight, management, and delivery of Local Government services in Education, Health, Water and Environment, and Agricu lture (micro -scale irrigation), including refugees and their host communities”. Specifically, the Programme sought to: 1. Increase the adequacy and predictability of fiscal transfers to Local Governments for service delivery; 2. Improve the equity and transparency of allocation mechanisms through the introduction of formula-based transfers; 3. Strengthen performance incentives and accountability systems for Local Governments; and 4. Expand access to quality education and health infrastructure, particularly in under-served areas. The UgIFT Programme had four components aimed at strengthening the intergovernmental fiscal transfer system while supporting investments in service delivery infrastructure. These included; Component 1: Reform of the Intergovernmental Fiscal Transfer System This supported the design and implementation of a reformed fiscal transfer framework based on objective and transparent allocation criteria. This resulted into introduction of formula -based grants - Revised allocation formulas reflecting population, infrastructure gaps, and service delivery needs. Component 2: Education Infrastructure Development This component financed the construction and upgrading of education facilities, particularly government secondary schools in under-served sub-counties. This involved construction and equipping of new secondary schools - classrooms, laboratories, administra tion blocks, sanitation facilities, teachers’ houses, furniture and ICT equipment in the different local governments.

Overall asset availability A total of 229,024 assets are recorded across the targeted MDAs, beneficiary Blood Banks, Upgraded Health Centres and Seed Secondary School. These include vehicles, laptops, printers, desktop computers, projectors, cameras, furniture (desks, chairs, tables and stools), UPS systems, digital phones, paper shredders, tablets and clinical equipment, among others. The quantitative tables use the current register codes: 215,504 assets marked Functional and in use, and 13,520 marked Faulty and not in use. The definitions below explain how quantities, condition and financial values are presented. Unresolved receipt, ownership and classification matters are included in the relevant schedules for follow-up. Term Meaning in this report Asset quantities Each entry represents one recorded unit. Totals include capitalized, expensed and unresolved entries; receipt and ownership exceptions require confirmation. Institution and location Assets are grouped by the institution and beneficiary to which they are attributed. Transfers, substitutions and uncertain programme assignments require reconciliation. Asset categories The categories describe the existing accounting classification. Known errors require correction before the categories can be treated as confirmed physical inventories. Recorded cost The available cost in Uganda shillings. Some amounts are estimates. A missing amount remains unresolved and is distinguished from a recorded zero. Service and purchase dates The service date is when the asset became available for use. The purchase date is a separate event and does not establish the service date. Useful life and salvage value Useful life is the period used for depreciation. Salvage value is the amount expected to remain at the end of that period. Neither determines when an asset physically fails. Depreciation Accumulated depreciation is the cost allocated over the asset’s accounting life to date. Year-to- date depreciation covers 1 July to 30 September 2026. Pending calculations remain unavailable. Net book value Recorded cost less accumulated depreciation for assets recognized for accounting purposes. Comparisons use the same records with all required amounts available. Recoverable amount An independently supported recoverable amount must be distinguished from a value based on net book value. The latter does not constitute an independent impairment valuation. Asset identification Asset references, programme markings, serial numbers and vehicle registrations help establish identity. Shared identifiers and missing markings require physical and custody checks. Condition and use Functional and Faulty are the two reported condition classes. Reasons for non-use are examined separately to determine whether installation, repair, replacement or disposal is appropriate. Complete accounting information Assets classified CAPITALIZED or construction in progress, with cost, accumulated depreciation and net book value all available.
